definitions.explanation: Not of the highest quality or rank. Used to describe people, things, or organizations that fall short of top-tier standards.

examples.japanese: {二流|にりゅう}⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{選手|せんしゅ}→選手：03823_senshu⟧⟦で→で：00502_de⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧⟦{勝|か}てない→勝つ：01199_katsu⟧。
⟦あの→あの：00915_ano⟧⟦{会社|かいしゃ}→会社：00607_kaisha⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧{二流|にりゅう}だ⟦と→と：00512_to⟧⟦{言|い}われている→言う：00515_iu⟧。
examples.english: That company is said to be second-rate.

examples.japanese: ⟦{一流|いちりゅう}→一流：03009_ichiryuu⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{技術|ぎじゅつ}→技術：01389_gijutsu⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦なくて→ない：01118_nai⟧⟦も→も：00484_mo⟧、{二流|にりゅう}⟦で→で：00502_de⟧{終|お}わりたく⟦ない→ない：01118_nai⟧⟦という→という：09577_toiu⟧{気持|きも}ち⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{大切|たいせつ}→大切：01456_taisetsu⟧だ。
examples.english: Even without top-tier skills, the desire not to end up second-rate is what matters.

notes:
USAGE:
{二流|にりゅう} is generally negative, implying that something or someone does not meet the highest standard. It is used with ⟦の→の：09472_no⟧ to modify nouns.
While {二流|にりゅう} literally means "second tier," it carries a negative connotation of being mediocre or not good enough. It is more blunt than ⟦{平凡|へいぼん}→平凡：12425_heibon⟧ (ordinary) and less harsh than {三流|さんりゅう}.

RELATED WORDS:
- ⟦{一流|いちりゅう}→一流：03009_ichiryuu⟧ (first-rate, top-class)
- {三流|さんりゅう} (third-rate, low-quality — more strongly negative)
- ⟦{超一流|ちょういちりゅう}→超一流：15580_chouichiryuu⟧ (world-class, top-tier)
